newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Fran runoff floods Washington D.C.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Fran runoff floods Washington D.C.

text.p: Floods from the swollen Potomac River forced the closing of key roads in and around Washington D.C. on Monday, snarling traffic in the aftermath of Hurricane Fran.
The river crested about 7 feet (2 metres) above flood stage in the upscale Georgetown neighborhood, swamping low-lying areas including a stretch of Constitution Avenue behind the White House.
No deaths or injuries were immediately reported.

The runoff forced the closing of heavily traveled parts of the George Washington Memorial Parkway, a key north-south artery that parallels the river and runs past the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts and National Airport.
Also closed were parts of Rock Creek Parkway, another key north-south thoroughfare.

The floods threatened repairs made to the historic C & O Canal pathway along the Potomac after a winter storm meltoff caused $25 million in damage in January. All park areas along the 184-mile-long (296 km-long) canal, which stretches from Cumberland, Maryland, to Georgetown, remained closed to the public, the Park Service said.
Fran, which tore through the Carolinas, Virginia and West Virginia last week, dumped 4 inches (10 cm) of rain in the capital city and up to 14 inches (36 cm) in outlying areas.
Thousands were forced out of their homes in the Shenandoah Valley region of Virginia over the weekend as the Shenandoah River rose 20 feet (six metres) above flood level.
